item.title: 'SC must review its order': TN Congress as top court directs deepam lighting at Deepathoon
item.description: Manickam Tagore, president of the Tamil Nadu Congress committee, has urged a review by the Supreme Court regarding its recent decision mandating the lighting of a ceremonial lamp at Madurai's Deepathoon stone pillar. This order has sparked concerns over federal principles, judiciary roles, and temple administration. Previous Supreme Court directives on security forces for the event's smooth execution have raised questions about the implications for religious harmony among communities.
item.dc:creator: Aastha Jha

item.title: Deepam lighting at Deepathoon today: CRPF deployed in TN's Thiruparankundram after SC order
item.description: In Thiruparankundram, CRPF personnel are on duty to ensure the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp is lit, following a Supreme Court order mandating the lamp's illumination at the Deepathoon stone pillar. This comes after previous issues with compliance. Under the court's directives, devotees can attend the ceremony, while the Tamil Nadu government has filed a review petition challenging the interim order.
item.dc:creator: Aastha Jha

item.title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
item.description: In an unexpected twist, the DMK is contemplating supporting the BJP on the delimitation bill after years of opposition. The BJP has offered several concessions to entice DMK's cooperation. This potential alliance highlights the complex and often shifting landscape of Indian politics, especially with the rise of Vijay's TVK, which narrows DMK's choices. Thus, political survival may compel them to forge an unlikely bond with the BJP.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Rakesh

item.title: Opposition mood despondent as NCP (SP), DMK change stand
item.description: The opposition faces a critical challenge with the proposed delimitation bill, as the DMK and NCP show support for it. Congress has raised alarms, accusing the BJP of trying to circumvent constitutional norms. After disappointing electoral results, there are fears of manipulated outcomes. Amid shifting alliances, Congress grapples with decisions that have upset DMK leadership, making the future of unity within the opposition uncertain.

item.title: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM
item.description: EAM S Jaishankar addressed the IORA, advocating for a unified global response to maritime attacks and ensuring safety. The joint communique emphasized respect for international law and commitments to maritime peace and stability. PM Narendra Modi engaged with foreign ministers from 23 member-states during the meeting to strengthen collaboration. India pledged $500,000 to enhance the association’s institutional and financial capacities for effective cooperation.

item.title: E-certificates for new citizens, hard copy on request
item.description: Individuals acquiring Indian citizenship will receive a digital certificate instead of a physical copy. This change applies to those registered or naturalised as citizens. Applicants can request a hard copy if desired, as per the new amendments. The digital certificates will be signed by an authorized officer from the central government. These amendments aim to modernize the process of issuing citizenship certificates in India.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain

item.title: Supreme Court junks plea seeking its intervention to remove Italian politician’s ‘vote chor’ remark on socials
item.description: The Supreme Court of India dismissed a plea concerning Giacomo Filibeck's remarks made during the Bharat Summit. The court stated that the petitioner could represent concerns to the Centre regarding regulations on foreign speeches. Filibeck's slogan and comments on Rahul Gandhi sparked controversy within political spaces. Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh emphasized the right to file complaints.

item.title: Killing at Rohtak eatery was directed from Georgia: Sleuths
item.description: Authorities are investigating gangster Ravi Rathi's suspected role in a shocking quadruple murder tied to his rival, Sunny Ritoli. Operating from Georgia, Rathi's henchmen employed a honeytrap to bait Ritoli into a lethal ambush at a hotel, resulting in the deaths of three aides while Ritoli narrowly escaped. Investigative teams are intensifying efforts to pinpoint Rathi's whereabouts, bracing for any retaliation as tensions escalate following the attack on Ritoli's crew.
item.dc:creator: Raj Shekhar Jha

item.title: CJI had sought probe against Jharkhand high court judge. He is Jhakhand acting chief justice now
item.description: CJI Surya Kant asked M S Sonak to investigate multiple complaints regarding Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad's integrity. Many of these complaints were supported by documentary evidence, which adds credibility to the claims. Complaints against Justice Prasad also reached Chief Minister Hemant Soren, who urged CJI Kant to address these concerns. Justice Prasad has held his position since 2014 but could face scrutiny due to the complaints received.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay.Mahapatra

item.title: Supreme Court raps TVK government, orders lamp lit at Tamil Nadu site today
item.description: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has reprimanded Tamil Nadu officials for their willful defiance of judicial orders. The court has now permitted all devotees to light lamps at the controversial location, expressing serious concern over the state's non-compliance and the initiation of contempt proceedings. Additionally, former judges have been appointed to supervise temple matters, reinforcing the importance of adhering to the rule of law.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Gavai cites two examples to buttress caste bias claim
item.description: B R Gavai expressed his apprehension regarding the Supreme Court's suggestion to transfer Justice M S Ramachandra Rao. Citing Rao's previous punitive transfers, Gavai questioned the wisdom in elevating a judge from a lesser high court to a more significant position. He warned that such actions could demoralize diligent judges within the judiciary, drawing from his own experiences in the collegium.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay Mahapatra

item.title: BJP says SC rebuke exposes Congress’s anti-Sanatan character
item.description: BJP president Nitin Nabin lauded the Supreme Court's decision to illuminate a ceremonial lamp in Thiruparankundram. He condemned the Tamil Nadu government's actions, implying they were driven by political motives. Nabin underscored the necessity of safeguarding the rights of worshippers and India's cultural heritage, asserting that no political agenda should interfere with the nation's sacred traditions, reinforcing the sanctity of constitutional values over partisan ideologies.

item.title: Collegium favouring caste that is 5% of population: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President
item.description: Ex-CJI B R Gavai has sharply criticized the current Supreme Court Collegium for ignoring diversity in judicial appointments. He expressed concerns about the favoring of one caste, potentially Brahmins, despite low population representation. His letter to President Droupadi Murmu urged accountability for these practices in the selection process. Gavai emphasized the need for proportional representation of marginalized communities in the judiciary.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay Mahapatra

item.title: Cabinet clears bills to raise 50% Lok Sabha seats across states, freeze delimitation till 2051
item.description: The Union Cabinet has given the green light to a new bill aimed at expanding the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats. This legislation introduces a significant milestone—a one-third reservation for women in both the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, set to commence in 2029. Additionally, it proposes a uniform 50% increase in constituencies across all states, based on the 2011 Census.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Rakesh and Dipak K Dash

item.title: Bisleri in fresh trouble: After Goa, FSSAI finds bacteria in West Bengal water sample
item.description: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has initiated prosecution against Bisleri International over unsafe drinking water samples. Recent tests revealed coliform bacteria in samples from its West Bengal and Goa plants. FSSAI has restricted the sale of specific batches following these findings and intensified surveillance on packaged drinking water quality. The regulator aims to ensure compliance with food safety norms across the country.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Saurav Das tells Piers Morgan show that he was born in Delhi and is Indian
item.description: Saurav Das addressed concerns regarding his nationality and mentioned he was born in Delhi. During an interview, he refuted discrepancies in his documents while asserting his family's Indian roots. Shazia Ilmi suggested documents had issues but later declared belief in his Indian citizenship. Das expressed frustration over allegations, which he viewed as attempts to undermine his activism.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Canton
